extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers / the general public
extracted.subtask_description: A multi-topic Associated Press newspaper page (Dec. 3, 1945) compiling national and international news briefs on legislation, courts, labor actions, military and postwar policy. The page reports facts, rulings and proposed legislative changes rather than offering how-to guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radio-license contested-applications hearing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When conflicting applications for a radio license show up, the Communications Commission must hear both before granting a permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supreme Court reversed the FCC where the commission had granted one application and set another for hearing because that procedure had the practical effect of nullifying the other applicant’s right to a hearing (case involved Fetzer Broadcasting Company and Ashbacker Radio Corporation). The Court did not pass on merits but enforced the right to hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hatch Act political-activity prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Hatch Act prohibits Federal employees from engaging in political activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes the Hatch Act’s prohibition in reporting discussion about exemptions and enforcement; it also mentions a contemporaneous proposal or discussion to exempt part-time Government employees from certain Hatch Act provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption proposal for part-time government employees (Hatch Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal/legislative language to exempt part-time Government employees from provisions of the Hatch Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as an item under consideration: an exemption of part-time Government employés from Hatch Act restrictions (context: debate over limits on Federal employee political activity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Court-martial specification formality standard
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not essential in a court-martial specification to assert that the accused committed a breach of a Federal statute or naval regulation; charges can be framed as negligence or 'culpable inefficiency' with specifications stating the facts (e.g., failing to order zigzag course, failing to issue timely orders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the opening of Capt. McVay’s general court-martial, the court overruled a motion to quash, stating the charges and specifications were in due form and technically correct and that it was unnecessary to allege a specific breach of statute/regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation criterion for surplus military equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Surplus jeeps and similar equipment would be allocated to regional RFC (Reconstruction Finance Corporation) offices and distributed in the various states on the basis of population and need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported in congressional discussion: Representative Case and others indicated that surplus jeeps would be allocated to regional RFC offices and that allotment among states would be on basis of population and need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government acceptance-of-gifts limitation (Gift Clause amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance of gifts made directly to the Government for furtherance of the war effort is confined to gifts made for the benefit of members of the armed forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The House amended the Gift Clause to restrict acceptance to gifts benefiting armed forces members; reported as a change in the law’s application for wartime-related gifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of authorities under the Second War Powers Act (extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Second War Powers Act (as amended/extended) includes authorities such as rationing and priorities over scarce materials, allocation and conservation of scarce materials, emergency powers of the Interstate Commerce Commission over coastal water carriers and motor vehicles, and commitments to supply foreign nations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The House/Senate extended most provisions (including rationing/priorities) until June 30, 1946; the article notes practical effects such as ending immediate government seizure of real estate before condemnation proceedings and continuation of powers needed for allocation of scarce materials and transport.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Senate two-thirds approval for international troop deployment
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed amendment would have required the Senate’s approval by a two-thirds majority before the President could allocate U.S. troops to an international police force (i.e., require supermajority Senate confirmation for such allocations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article reports the amendment by Senator (Dom?) which sought to require Senate approval by two-thirds for presidential allocation of U.S. forces to international bodies; the amendment was debated and defeated (vote figures noted in the reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative-procedure constraint: procedures must not nullify right to hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative procedures that have the practical effect of nullifying a party’s statutory right to a hearing cannot stand; agencies must afford an actual hearing when the law contemplates one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived from the Supreme Court’s reversal of the FCC action in the Fetzer/Ashbacker matter: even if an agency has discretion, it cannot adopt a procedure that effectively deprives an applicant of the hearing to which the statute entitles them.
